newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude slips, spreads come off.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude slips, spreads come off.

text.p: North Sea crude slipped sharply late on Tuesday, shedding earlier gains, as traders dismissed expectations Shell's export problems in Nigeria would have a major impact on supplies.
June Brent was 22 cents a barrel weaker at $18.12 by 1715 GMT after dipping to a low of $18.03, way off the day's high of $18.64.

The contract, which was pushed up on Shell Nigeria's declaration of a force majeure on exports from its Nigerian Bonny terminal because of a contractors' strike there, lost ground in late trade after NYMEX's WTI contract dipped.

Shell's Nigerian group said on Tuesday it was making arrangements to restore crude loadings at Bonny and should have supporting craft arriving there on Thursday which would mean they could restore loadings even if the strike continued.

There were no cargoes loading at Bonny terminal, traders said. One trader, who was due to start loading a VLCC of Bonny Light and Forcados on Monday, said that NNPC had requested his vessel to load Forcados first.
"It seems a sensible way of dealing with a problem which will probably not last very long," another regular loader said.

Both Brent cargoes from Tuesday's chains were five o' clocked. Meanwhile, with the last two April cargoes heading for the U.S. on an LR2, differentials were firming, traders said. The cargoes were bought on Monday at June Brent -50 cents. An early May Brent was offered at June -35 cents with buyers 10 cents lower.
Brent intermonth spreads weakened slightly on the back of the Brent fall. May/June was talked at -17/-15 and Jun/Jul -7/-5 cts.
